meaning.evidence: All actions, figures, votes and dates kept; the directive and statement quotations are left verbatim, as they should be. "help bring inflation back to the Committee's 2 percent goal sooner" renders "timelier".

sense.evidence: "hardly budged", "at a solid clip", "dead set on hitting", "gave the nod" all fit their contexts.

authenticity.evidence: Natural Australian ("stuck by", "made it plain", "put the target range for the federal funds rate up"), but keeps US "percent" in its own narration, and "give a 1/4 percentage point increase in the primary credit rate the nod" is a forced construction.

register.evidence: For level 4 it is light: the narrative paragraphs have touches like "at a solid clip" and "wrapped up", but much reads as plain prose ("Members noted the unemployment rate had hardly budged"). No swearing, which vulgarity 1 permits.

tone.evidence: Keeps the measured, official tone of minutes: "The Committee made it plain it's still dead set on hitting its dual-mandate goals".

flow.evidence: Mostly smooth; "voted unanimously to give a 1/4 percentage point increase in the primary credit rate the nod, taking it to 4.0 percent" is long-winded.

variety.evidence: "the nod" twice ("gave the nod", "the nod, taking it") and "wrapped up" twice ("Once the discussion wrapped up", "The meeting wrapped up").

essence.evidence: Still clearly the FOMC minutes section, with structure intact.

problems.quote: all members agreed to put the target range for the federal funds rate up 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent
problems.original: all members agreed to raise the target range for the federal funds rate 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent
problems.why: US spelling percent left in the narration where Australian would write per cent.

problems.quote: voted unanimously to give a 1/4 percentage point increase in the primary credit rate the nod
problems.original: voted unanimously to approve a 1/4 percentage point increase in the primary credit rate
problems.why: Split idiom around a long noun phrase is clunky.

problems.quote: Members noted the unemployment rate had hardly budged
problems.original: Members noted that the unemployment rate was largely unchanged
problems.why: Register light for a level-4 brief; much of the narration stays near plain English.

A.summary: Accurate and natural but lighter than a level-4 brief asks.

meaning.evidence: Facts and numbers kept, but "Members reckoned the unemployment rate had barely budged" turns an observation into an opinion, and "doubled down on the FOMC's policy" overstates "reaffirmed". It also changes "percent" to "per cent" inside the quoted directive and statement, altering an official quotation.

sense.evidence: "doubled down" takes the wrong sense (escalating, not reaffirming); "reckoned" strains for "noted". "give the tick", "signed off" and "done and dusted" fit.

authenticity.evidence: Lively and mostly natural ("kept chugging along at a solid clip", "put it in black and white"), though "doubled down" is an Americanism.

register.evidence: Closest to level 4 in the narration: "every member gave the nod to bumping", "Once the talking was done and dusted", "get together next". No swearing (permitted at vulgarity 1).

tone.evidence: Slightly jaunty for central-bank minutes ("Once the talking was done and dusted"), but the change of voice is what the brief asks; tone mostly holds.

flow.evidence: Reads well, though "gave the nod to bumping the target range for the federal funds rate up" stacks idioms.

variety.evidence: Good range, with some reuse: "signed off" twice ("signed off on the statement", "signed off on the minutes") and "to go out at 2:00 p.m." twice.

essence.evidence: Recognisable throughout; the retitled heading "What the Committee Did" is the only structural change.

problems.quote: they doubled down on the FOMC's policy of keeping ample reserves
problems.original: reaffirmed the FOMC's policy of maintaining ample reserves
problems.why: Doubling down means escalating a commitment, often stubbornly; the original only reaffirms it. Also an Americanism.

problems.quote: Members reckoned the unemployment rate had barely budged
problems.original: Members noted that the unemployment rate was largely unchanged
problems.why: Reckoned makes a factual observation sound like an opinion.

problems.quote: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 3-3/4 to 4 per cent.
problems.original: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 3-3/4 to 4 percent.
problems.why: Alters the wording of a verbatim official quotation.

B.summary: Most on-brief in weight, but one wrong-sense idiom and a few liberties.

meaning.evidence: All facts kept; quotations left verbatim; "per cent" used in narration only. "help get inflation back to the Committee's 2 per cent goal sooner".

sense.evidence: "barely shifted", "running high", "dead set on hitting", "give a 1/4 percentage point increase the nod" all carry the right sense.

authenticity.evidence: Natural where it uses Aussie, with "per cent" localised; "The same vote also took in sign-off on the statement below" is unidiomatic.

register.evidence: Lightest of the three: many sentences are near the original ("At the end of the discussion, the Committee voted to direct the Federal Reserve Bank of New York"). Well under level 4. No swearing (permitted).

tone.evidence: Keeps the formal tone of minutes intact.

flow.evidence: Some clunky lines: "solid growth in economic activity had kept on" and "The same vote also took in sign-off on the statement below".

variety.evidence: Little repetition, though there is little slang to repeat: "the nod", "bump up", "signed off", "wrapped up".

problems.quote: The same vote also took in sign-off on the statement below for release at 2:00 p.m.
problems.original: The vote also encompassed approval of the statement below for release at 2:00 p.m.

problems.quote: solid growth in economic activity had kept on
problems.original: solid growth in economic activity had continued
problems.why: Kept on without a following verb reads as broken.

problems.quote: At the end of the discussion, the Committee voted to direct the Federal Reserve Bank of New York
problems.original: At the conclusion of the discussion, the Committee voted to direct the Federal Reserve Bank of New York
problems.why: Register well short of level 4; much of the narration is barely changed.

C.summary: Accurate and careful but too light for the brief, with a couple of clunky joins.
